vuln_id: knot-dns libzscanner SVCB/HTTPS output overflow / ARVO arvo:37151

project.name: Knot DNS
project.commit_note: The sample metadata leaves `vulnerable_commit` empty. The exact staged vulnerable checkout under `gt_results/arvo_37151/_work/src/knot-dns` is commit `b5713e263f7f4b1a92835943102cf2976ae4f7d1`; its libzscanner SVCB/HTTPS parser matches the staged patch hunks and the saved ASan line map.

classification.classification_note: The witnessed manifestation is a 2-byte out-of-bounds stack write past `zs_scanner_t.r_data[65535]` while serializing an empty trailing HTTPS/SVCB parameter.

bug_description.original: A missing output buffer overflow check in the SVCB processing of libzscanner allows for potential buffer overflows.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 65548-byte witness is a textual `TYPE65` (HTTPS) record whose rdata is `9`, target `G.`, a generic `key0=` value of 65520 text bytes, then empty `key6` and `key3` parameters. `parse()` serializes HTTPS/SVCB parameters into the fixed stack buffer `zs_scanner_t.r_data[65535]`. After the 5-byte `9 G.` prefix and the oversized `key0` param, `key6` exactly consumes the next 4 bytes and leaves only two buffer bytes unused. The vulnerable `_svcb_param_init` action still accepts the trailing `key3` without checking that another 4-byte `{key,len}` header fits. `_num16_write` stores key 3 into the last two bytes, then `svcb_empty` writes a 2-byte zero value length past the end of `r_data`, producing the observed AddressSanitizer stack-buffer-overflow at `scanner.c:8136`.

source.description: First project-code materialization of attacker data into vulnerability-relevant parser state: the numeric suffix of the witness token `TYPE65` is stored as record type 65/HTTPS, which is the only reason the later rdata dispatch enters the vulnerable SVCB/HTTPS parameter parser.
source.value_from: The staged witness `gt_results/arvo_37151/poc` is exactly 65548 bytes (sha256 `5d2e137fc5580be98e56c1c5d0cf60b337817f1ca4322f28a912d87256e01f49`). Splitting it on tabs yields six fields: `4`, `TYPE65 9`, `G`, `key0=<65520-byte text>`, `key6`, and `key3`. The `TYPE65` token is parsed through the generic `TYPE` path and reaches this assignment with `s->number64 == 65`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. When a new HTTPS/SVCB parameter starts, `_svcb_param_init` records the current output pointer but does not verify that the mandatory 4-byte `{key,len}` header still fits in `r_data`.
root_cause.note: On the witnessed path this action runs for trailing `key3` with only two bytes left in the buffer. The fix patch adds `if (rdata_tail + 4 > rdata_stop + 1) { WARN(ZS_RDATA_OVERFLOW); ... }` at this exact site, which would reject `key3` before any further writes.

sink.description: Sink. This generated `%_write16_0` body stores the 2-byte zero value length for the empty trailing `key3` parameter after `rdata_tail` has already been advanced to the one-past-end pointer of `r_data`.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports the crash at `/src/knot-dns/src/libzscanner/scanner.c:8136:3` with `WRITE of size 2`. The staged vulnerable tree contains the matching generated source at `src/libzscanner/scanner.c.t0:8136`, and `Makefile.inc` copies `scanner.c.t0` to `scanner.c` when `FAST_PARSER` is not enabled.

tainted_value_origin.description: The size-driving attacker value is the witness's `key0=` generic parameter text. Its payload is exactly 65520 bytes, so serializing that one parameter moves the HTTPS/SVCB output cursor near the end of the fixed 65535-byte `r_data` buffer before the trailing empty parameters are parsed.

parser_admitted.description: After `TYPE65` sets `s->r_type` to HTTPS, `_text_r_data` dispatches this witness into `r_data_svcb`. The preceding `9` priority and target `G` satisfy the `num16 . sep . r_dname` prefix, so the remaining input reaches `svcb_params` on the tokens `key0=<65520-byte text>`, `key6`, and `key3`.

fine_trace.note: Source. The witness token `TYPE65` is parsed through the generic type-number path and stores `65` into `s->r_type`, creating the HTTPS record-type state that selects the vulnerable SVCB/HTTPS rdata parser.

The HTTPS/SVCB rdata grammar serializes the witness's priority `9` and target `G.` before parameter parsing. Those fields occupy 5 bytes in `s->r_data`, and `scanner.h` fixes the whole destination buffer at 65535 bytes, so `svcb_params` starts at offset 5 and can use bytes 5 through 65534.

The first param token `key0=<65520-byte text>` takes the non-empty generic-value arm. `svcb_key_generic` writes key 0, `_item_length2_init` reserves a 2-byte value-length slot, `text` copies 65520 bytes, and `_item_length2_exit` backfills that length. Starting from step 2's offset 5, this moves `rdata_tail` to offset 65529.

The next token `key6` is a generic param with an empty value, so it serializes as a 2-byte key plus the 2-byte zero value length from `svcb_empty`. From offset 65529 this exactly consumes four more bytes and advances `rdata_tail` to offset 65533, leaving only the final two buffer bytes unused.

Root cause on the trailing token `key3`. This action runs with `rdata_tail == s->r_data + 65533`, so only two bytes remain in `r_data`. The vulnerable code still accepts the param and records its start instead of first rejecting the missing 4-byte `{key,len}` capacity.

The digits in the trailing token `key3` materialize as `s->number64 == 3`, and `_num16_write` stores that key code into the last two buffer bytes at offsets 65533 and 65534. After this write, `rdata_tail` equals `s->r_data + 65535`, i.e. the one-past-end pointer `rdata_stop + 1`.

Sink. `key3` has no `=` value, so the parser takes `svcb_empty` and `%_write16_0` tries to store the 2-byte zero value length at the one-past-end pointer from step 6. The saved ASan trace reports this exact 2-byte WRITE at `/src/knot-dns/src/libzscanner/scanner.c:8136:3`.

crash_stack.function: fuzzer::FuzzerDriver(int*, char***, int (*)(unsigned char const*, unsigned long))

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: On the witnessed path, the relevant fix is the new `_svcb_param_init` check `if (rdata_tail + 4 > rdata_stop + 1)` added in `scanner_body.rl`. With the staged witness, `key6` leaves `rdata_tail == s->r_data + 65533`, so the patched build would reject the trailing empty `key3` before `_num16_write` and `%_write16_0` run. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.

format.name: 65548-byte TYPE65 HTTPS/SVCB witness
format.contract: The staged witness is exactly the 65548-byte file `gt_results/arvo_37151/poc` (sha256 `5d2e137fc5580be98e56c1c5d0cf60b337817f1ca4322f28a912d87256e01f49`). Splitting it on tabs yields `4`, `TYPE65 9`, `G`, `key0=<65520-byte text>`, `key6`, and `key3`. In `r_data_svcb`, the 5-byte `9 G.` prefix plus the serialized `key0` param leave `rdata_tail` at offset 65529; empty `key6` advances it to 65533; the vulnerable code still accepts empty `key3`, writes its 2-byte key into the last two bytes, and then crashes while writing the 2-byte zero value length. No broader HTTPS/SVCB input class beyond this exact witnessed layout is claimed here.
